name: aida_r5_dining_towel
purpose: A cotton towel hung over a drying rail in the dining room, a corner hanging free at reach height: the R5 stands before the rail, reaches forward, pinches the hanging corner with its left hand, lifts it 20 cm and holds. The first cloth experiment: does a PhysX surface deformable stay in the Ability Hand's pinch?
physics_hz_why: the hand firmware per physics step as before, at 240 Hz: cloth at 480 Hz doubles the cost of every trial; 240 Hz is a 4 ms stall loop

environment.fixtures_why: a wall-mounted drying rail between the table's end (x 5.807) and the east wall (x 6.9), its top at 0.98 m; the towel hangs over it with both faces free; the rail runs y 0.60-1.40 so the robot's front (y 0.52) is clear of it (a rail from 0.50 ran into the chassis at 0.95 m)
environment.support_why: the rail is the support: a towel hanging over a table's edge put the hem 13 cm below a 0.71 m top, and from some twenty robot placements the arm could not present a pinch across the sheet there (the digit behind the flap under the slab, or no IK with the closing axis near the sheet's normal); over a rail the hem hangs at 0.67 m with nothing behind it

objects.name: Towel
objects.label: the blue towel
objects.why: 0.30 x 0.40 m, its long side across the rail: 12 cm hangs on the +x side and 28 cm on the robot's side (-x), so the long flap's hem is at about 0.67 m; its -y corner is the one nearest the robot

cloth_grip.tolerance_why: a 1.5 mm sheet is sandwiched only by a pinch close to its normal (at 60 deg the tips closed beside the sheet)

grasp_plan.lift_out_why: drawn 5 cm away from the rail at the pinch height first (the flap off the rail's face), then up 20 cm
grasp_plan.why: the long flap's -y corner, 2.5 cm in from the corner and 1 cm up from its hem, pinched across the cloth; drawn off the rail, then the palm straight up 20 cm; the rail as a slab band (support_geometry.py)

hand_model.why: the grip command with the ICD's post-contact voltage (misc word 008) at 1.5 V: on cloth a digit halts tip-to-tip with the fabric between the pads at the 3 V threshold, and at 0 V the worm then holds only the pad squeeze stored at that instant - the pinch closed on the corner and let it go 2 cm into the draw-out (2026-10-15). With 1.5 V after contact the digits keep closing in as the cloth shifts, as the real hand does with the setting; the can held at 1.5 V and dropped at 0 V the same way

robot.placement_why: before the rail's near end, facing along it (+y; CAD forward is -Y, yaw 180 faces world +Y): the towel's flap hangs on the robot's left (-x), its plane along the forward reach, its normal the robot's lateral axis - a lateral pinch in a forward reach
robot.posture_why: HomeHero's navigation rest as the base spec, the head panned to look ahead at the table's end (the side-table posture panned it 88 deg left); a one-level spec merge replaces the whole posture dict, so it is carried in full

overview_camera.why: from the room's south-west, ahead and to the robot's left: the robot's front-left, its left arm, the rail and the hanging towel (a camera behind the robot filmed its back panels, 2026-10-15)

extra_cameras.name: GraspCloseup
extra_cameras.why: from the robot's left-front at hand height: the flap, the pinch and the lift
